title: Adaptive Hitmap Architect and Rollforward Procedures for KV Prefix Caching
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: produce an automated recommendation engine and safe deployment flow that proposes per-prefix cache key designs, TTL ladders, and batching-aware policies to reduce token spend while preserving latency SLOs and output quality. Deliverables: 1) hitmap estimator service that infers per-prefix hit curves from streaming telemetry; 2) TTL/policy scorer that outputs conservative, medium, and aggressive configs; 3) simulation harness to predict cost/hitrate/latency trade-offs under realistic batch/sequence distributions; 4) staged apply & rollback runner integrated with the console's rollout workflows and alerting; 5) documentation and runbook for operators and SREs.
success_criteria: Net hosted token-cost reduction >= 12% for target workloads at <= 1% increase in tail latency (p99). Staged rollout must detect and revert within 15 minutes for regressions over defined thresholds. Recommendations should produce stable hit-rate forecasts (RMSE < 6 percentage points) in shadow replays.
deliverables: ttl-policy-scorer with 3 risk profiles and confidence scoring
simulation harness (traffic replay + synthetic surge scenarios)
staged-apply runner with canary, ramp, and auto-revert
technical_notes: We intentionally avoided heavy neural models for hit prediction due to explainability and compute cost. Final estimator is a Bayesian hierarchical model with per-prefix priors seeded from sampling; for very sparse prefixes we fallback to a cohort-level baseline. TTLs are expressed in a discrete ladder (5m, 30m, 1h, 6h, 24h) to simplify rollout and metrics aggregation. Batching-aware adjustments: the scorer penalizes policies that sharply increase median tokens-per-request or that would push KV lookups into large synchronous batches on tail traffic patterns.

decisions: Use hierarchical Bayesian estimator seeded by sampled telemetry (better uncertainty estimates than LR).
TTL choices will be constrained to a discrete ladder to limit combinatorial explosion of configs.
Apply flow will only enable 'aggressive' profile with manual approval for accounts flagged as high-SLA.
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: 1) p99 latency increase > 1.0% absolute AND 2) KV error rate increase > 0.2% within a 30-minute window OR 3) hit-rate drop > 6 percentage points for the canary cohort. Rollback mechanics: a) staged-apply runner immediately posts revert and sets policy to previous stable config; b) operator notified via Slack and incident runbook (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Cache+Policy+Rollback); c) automated forensic snapshot stored (playback and telemetry links included). Manual fallback: if auto-revert fails, run 'cfg-revert --account <id> --policy previous' on ops-runner host.
